newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Great Ocean says competition hit profit.
newsitem.headline: Great Ocean says competition hit profit.

text.p: China's Shenzhen Great Ocean Shipping Co said on Thursday its 1996 net profit was sharply down on the 1995 figure because of sharpened competition and a sluggish market.

Net profit slumped to 35.631 million yuan in 1996, down 29.75 percent from 50.72 million yuan in 1995 based on international accouting standards, the company said in an annual report published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
"1996 was a turbulent year for the shipping business," the company said.
The company attributed its 1996 performance to China's shrinking export market which it said had forced many shipping companies to sharply cut prices.
Cuts in export and import tax rebates, the yuan's strength against the U.S. dollar and inflation squeezed China's export market, it said.

The company's turnover was 176.1 million yuan in 1996 compared with 164.6 million yuan in 1995 under international accounting standards, its annual report published in Thursday's South China Morning Post said.
Foreign shipping companies entering China's market also tightened competition, the annual report published in Shenzhen said.
The board of directors is very confident that net profit will recover significantly in 1997, a company official said.

Two new ships, which went into operation late last year, are likely to boost the company's 1997 and 1998 results, which would also be lifted by an issue of 50 million B shares expected in April, he said.
The company has received preliminary approval to offer the shares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, the official said, adding that J&A Securities (Hong Kong) is the chief international underwriter.
It would use proceeds from the offer, tentatively priced at between HK$2.50 and HK$3.50 per share, to buy container ships, the company has said.
Great Ocean listed 72 million B shares at the end of 1996.
It planned to cut costs, broaden its market and restructure its operations, Great Ocean said but gave no further details.
